You're interested in the nitty-gritty of the MITRE Att&CK framework, eh?

T1566.001 is an attack technique in the "Phishing" tactic, specifically related to "Sending Phishing Messages ( via Web Application)".

In this attack, an adversary sends a malicious message to the victim through a web application, attempting to trick the user into divulging sensitive information or executing malicious actions. This can be done by crafting a fake login page, a suspicious link, or even a cleverly designed email notification that appears to come from a trusted source.

For instance, I've seen this technique used on our server when I noticed some suspicious traffic coming in on port 443 (HTTPS) from an unknown IP address. Upon investigation, I found an attempt to exploit a vulnerability in our web application to send a phishing email to our users, trying to get them to reveal their credentials.

To prevent such attacks, we have our web application firewall (WAF) configured to block traffic to port 443 from suspicious IP addresses. We're running an NGINX web server (nginx/1.24.0) with a strict configuration, including rate limiting and IP blocking, on our Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server with kernel 5.
